novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism-level phenomenon—“even without any mechanistic supervision, these models internally encode the arrow-pushing electron-redistribution structure”—in standard Molecular Transformer and Chemformer product predictors, with the additional hypothesis that this representation is “causally load-bearing,” rather than merely introducing a new setting. The closest prior work is FlowER, “Electron flow matching for generative reaction mechanism prediction” (Nature, 2025), while searches using “Molecular Transformer implicit electron flow,” “Chemformer mechanistic representation,” “reaction transformer electron donor acceptor probing,” “bond-electron matrix activation probing,” and “causal steering chemistry transformer” found mechanistic models that impose electron flow and interpretability studies of chemical substructures, but no equivalent test of latent electron-flow structure in unsupervised product-prediction transformers. The step from FlowER and related work to this claim requires a new core relationship—whether recipe-trained models spontaneously represent and causally use directional electron redistribution—rather than a direct transfer or mere renaming of probing, SAEs, or activation steering, supporting a high-within-framework novelty score rather than paradigm-level novelty.
